reviews.scope: Astro documentation; official UI integrations named where required.

ssr.note: On-demand rendering uses an official deployment adapter, such as @astrojs/node.
ssr.label: SSR adapter

streaming.note: On-demand Astro pages stream HTML; deployed adapters and proxies must preserve streaming.

suspense.note: server:defer renders fallback UI, then fetches each server island from a separate endpoint. This is not a React-style boundary inside the original HTML stream.
suspense.label: Server islands

client.note: client:* directives activate islands using UI integrations such as @astrojs/react and @astrojs/vue.
client.label: UI islands

ssg.note: Pages are prerendered at build time by default; server mode can opt individual routes into prerendering.

csr.note: client:only skips server rendering for a supported UI framework component. Astro components themselves have no client rendering runtime.
csr.label: client:only / UI integration

serverOnly.note: Astro components execute on the server/build and send no component runtime by default. UI islands use separate integrations.
serverOnly.label: Astro components

partialRendering.note: server:defer combines a prerendered page with separately fetched server islands, not one request-time HTML stream.
partialRendering.label: Separate island requests

routing.note: Files under src/pages define page and endpoint routes.

layouts.note: Layouts are ordinary Astro components explicitly composed through slots and props; no automatic route-layout inheritance is implied.

dynamicRoutes.note: Bracketed page filenames accept parameters; static routes enumerate paths and on-demand routes resolve at request time.

parallelRoutes.note: The reviewed page/endpoint router has no documented independently navigable named-slot API comparable to parallel routes.

interceptedRoutes.note: ClientRouter supports transitions/navigation, but the reviewed guide does not define a routed-modal interception/direct-link contract.

prefetch.note: Optional prefetch supports hover, tap, viewport, or load strategies; the client router also coordinates navigation.

softNavigation.note: Opt-in ClientRouter intercepts internal navigation, swaps HTML and updates history. Persistent elements and lifecycle events are supported; scripts and islands must follow the documented navigation lifecycle.
softNavigation.label: ClientRouter

viewTransitions.note: ClientRouter and transition directives coordinate page/shared-element animations and persistence. Browser support, fallback behavior and reduced-motion preferences affect the result; the feature is opt-in.
viewTransitions.label: astro:transitions

redirects.note: Astro.redirect and configured redirects are supported, with output dependent on static hosting or adapter capabilities.

serverData.note: Component scripts await fetch at build time or on demand; browser fetching uses client scripts or UI libraries.

clientData.note: Client scripts or UI-framework islands can fetch again in the browser; Astro does not document a built-in browser query-cache API here.
clientData.label: UI island / app code

requestDedupe.note: The reviewed fetch/data-loading guide does not establish automatic equivalently keyed request deduplication. Route caching is a separate boundary.

persistentCache.note: Astro 7 route caching retains on-demand responses using an explicit provider; built-in memory storage and adapter-specific providers are documented.
persistentCache.label: Astro 7 route cache

invalidation.note: Astro.cache.invalidate targets paths or tags; provider capabilities determine the runtime purge implementation.
invalidation.label: Path / tag invalidation

isr.note: The documented route cache stores on-demand HTML with maxAge/SWR and explicit invalidation. It requires a compatible server adapter/cache provider; a static-only export cannot regenerate pages on request.
isr.label: Route-cache SWR

apiRoutes.note: Endpoints produce arbitrary responses; on-demand server endpoints support HTTP methods.

actions.note: Astro Actions expose typed server handlers to browser code and HTML forms.
actions.label: Astro Actions

forms.note: Actions parse and validate form/JSON input with schemas and expose typed browser callers.

assessment.summary: Form transport, validation, pending feedback and optimistic state are separate behaviors; the progressive-forms and optimistic-updates rows review the latter contracts explicitly.
strengths: Actions parse and validate form/JSON input with schemas and expose typed browser callers.
tradeoffs: Do not infer a no-JavaScript submission path, automatic validation, accessible field errors or rollback merely from the ability to receive FormData.

middleware.note: Middleware wraps page/endpoint rendering and shares request data through locals.

cookies.note: Server-side sessions store data between on-demand requests; storage and adapter configuration affect deployment.
cookies.label: Sessions

cssModules.note: Vite-backed CSS Module imports provide generated local class names.

scopedCss.note: Component style tags are scoped by default; global selectors/styles can opt out.

tailwind.note: The documented Tailwind setup uses its external Vite plugin.
tailwind.label: Tailwind / Vite

cssInJs.note: The reviewed styling guide establishes Astro scoped CSS and UI-framework CSS processing, but no Astro-owned CSS-in-JS runtime/SSR registry.

images.note: Image, Picture, and image generation APIs transform sources; responsive resizing and services are configurable.

fonts.note: A typed font API supports local/provider sources, preload links, optimized fallbacks, and generated font assets.

scripts.note: Component scripts are bundled/deduplicated or inlined. A next/script-style strategy scheduler is not established here.
scripts.label: Bundled scripts

assetPipeline.note: Assets imported from source enter Astro’s Vite build graph: production URLs are hashed or small files are inlined, and references are updated. Files in public/ are copied unchanged and need their own versioning and cache policy.
assetPipeline.label: Vite asset imports

staticAssets.note: Public files are copied without transformation; imported source images can go through the image pipeline.

metadata.note: The guide composes an application-owned BaseHead component and passes props. This is not a structured, automatically merged metadata registry.
metadata.label: Application-owned pattern

assessment.label: Application-owned pattern
assessment.summary: Flexible head composition through normal components and props; the application defines its metadata contract.
strengths: A shared head component can be reused across layouts and receive typed application props.
tradeoffs: The reviewed layout guide does not establish automatic metadata-object inheritance, deduplication, or child-override rules.
Additional SEO behavior must be implemented or supplied by an integration.

dynamicMetadata.note: Pages can pass data into a shared head/layout component. The application owns the metadata composition contract.
dynamicMetadata.label: App-owned composition

metadataInheritance.note: Layouts compose explicit props and slots. The reviewed layout API does not define automatic metadata-field inheritance.

metadataOverrides.note: A reusable head component can implement custom overrides; no standard metadata-object merge/clear contract is documented here.

titleTemplates.note: Applications can format a title prop, but the reviewed layout API has no dedicated ancestor title-template/absolute-title API.

socialImages.note: astro-og-canvas generates Open Graph images from page data through an Astro endpoint; it is a separate integration.
socialImages.label: astro-og-canvas

sitemaps.note: @astrojs/sitemap generates sitemaps from static routes, with configuration for extra pages; server-only dynamic URLs need explicit inclusion.
sitemaps.label: @astrojs/sitemap

robots.note: Publish an application-authored robots.txt from public or an endpoint. A typed crawler-directive generator is not established.
robots.label: Public file / endpoint

markdown.note: Markdown includes frontmatter and component rendering; MDX requires the separate official integration.
markdown.label: Markdown; MDX package

collections.note: Typed collections validate and query local/remote content through loaders and schemas.

draftMode.note: Live collections are documented for immediate CMS draft previews. Preview authentication and cache bypass policy remain application/CMS-owned.
draftMode.label: Live-collection workflow

translations.note: The documented recipe uses application-owned translation dictionaries. Astro's i18n routing is separate from message translation.
translations.label: Dictionary recipe

localeRouting.note: Locale configuration, URL helpers, preferred-language detection, and fallback routing; domain routing has prerendering restrictions.

localeFormatting.note: Astro’s reviewed i18n API manages locales/URLs; a locale-aware number/date formatting API is not documented.

auth.note: The guide provides Astro integrations for services/libraries including Better Auth and Clerk; identity management is external.
auth.label: Better Auth / Clerk

csp.note: Astro 6+ can emit a CSP meta policy with processed script/style hashes and runtime customization. This differs from a complete application-authored HTTP header policy.
csp.label: Meta CSP / hashes

cspNonce.note: Astro's reviewed CSP integration coordinates script/style hashes in a meta policy. It does not establish a per-response nonce pipeline for generated scripts; the hash-based CSP capability is recorded in its own row.
cspNonce.label: Hash-based CSP instead

csrf.note: Default origin/site checks protect on-demand unsafe requests with the documented form/simple content types. This is not a universal CSRF-token service.
csrf.label: Origin/site checks

environment.note: astro:env validates a schema and separates public/client values from server secrets.

types.note: TypeScript authoring is supported; astro check plus its official checker validates Astro/TS sources. Building alone does not perform the same checks.
types.label: astro check

hmr.note: The development server updates changed source/assets through Vite; framework-island state behavior depends on its integration.
hmr.label: Vite development

cli.note: Astro’s CLI supplies dev, build, preview, check, and project tooling commands.

bundleAnalysis.note: The official recipe adds rollup-plugin-visualizer to inspect module sizes and dependency composition.
bundleAnalysis.label: rollup-plugin-visualizer

unitTests.note: The guide integrates external runners and component-testing tools.
unitTests.label: Vitest / test libraries

e2eTests.note: Browser testing uses external Playwright or Cypress integrations.
e2eTests.label: Playwright / Cypress

observability.note: Astro 7 exposes configurable logger destinations, request flush hooks, and console/structured logging integration. Metrics/tracing backends remain separate.
observability.label: Logger API

errorHandling.note: Custom 404/500 pages handle route errors; UI-island component error boundaries depend on the UI framework.
errorHandling.label: Error pages / UI integration

serverHosting.note: On-demand hosting requires a deployment adapter such as the official Node adapter.
serverHosting.label: SSR adapter

staticHosting.note: The default build produces static files for static hosting; on-demand features require an adapter.

containers.note: The official Docker recipe covers static and Node-adapter images. The application owns its Dockerfile and deployment.

edgeHosting.note: Official adapter paths include Cloudflare; runtime feature support depends on the adapter.
edgeHosting.label: Cloudflare adapter

client.note: Fullstack supports hydration of the server-rendered application.
client.label: Hydration

ssg.label: Fullstack SSG

csr.note: The web target renders and updates UI in the browser through the WASM runtime.

serverOnly.note: Server-only blocks and server functions stay on the server; normal Fullstack components also execute during browser hydration.
serverOnly.label: Server blocks / functions

partialRendering.note: The reviewed static/incremental renderer does not establish a prebuilt shell with per-request dynamic UI holes.

routing.note: The fullstack server integrates an Axum router and registers server functions.
routing.label: Fullstack / Axum

layouts.note: The official Router nests routes inside layout components with Outlet.
layouts.label: Dioxus Router

dynamicRoutes.note: Routable derives typed dynamic, catch-all, query, and hash route segments.
dynamicRoutes.label: Dioxus Router

parallelRoutes.note: Nested Outlet layouts are documented, but not independently navigable named route slots.

interceptedRoutes.note: The reviewed navigation guide does not define intercepted-modal and direct-link rendering semantics.

prefetch.note: Link and Navigator navigation are documented; automatic route/data prefetch is not established by the reviewed guide.

softNavigation.note: dioxus-router Link/Navigator update internal routed UI and history without fetching a new document. External navigation can leave the application; the router also serves non-browser targets.

viewTransitions.note: The reviewed routing API does not establish this navigation capability. Application code or another package may provide it; this finding is not proof of absence.

redirects.note: Navigator and router callbacks can replace/redirect navigation; server responses can separately set HTTP redirects.
redirects.label: Dioxus Router

serverData.note: use_loader resolves data during SSR and serializes its result for the initial client render.
serverData.label: Fullstack use_loader

reviews.scope: Next.js App Router documentation, including its React integration.

ssr.note: App Router renders Server Components and initial page HTML on the server.

streaming.note: loading.js and Suspense stream HTML as route segments or components resolve.

suspense.note: React Suspense boundaries display fallback UI while App Router streams resolved content.

client.note: React hydration activates Client Components; Suspense enables selective hydration.
client.label: React hydration

ssg.note: Static export generates an HTML file per route. Server-dependent features are unavailable in a static-only deployment.

csr.note: Client Components render subsequent navigations in the browser. Initial visits still receive prerendered HTML.

serverOnly.note: React Server Components keep server implementation and dependencies out of the client bundle. Serialized props still reach the browser.
serverOnly.label: React Server Components

partialRendering.note: Cache Components combines a prerendered shell with request-time streaming. Existing apps must enable the documented configuration.
partialRendering.label: Cache Components

routing.note: App Router uses files, nested layouts, page segments, and route handlers.

layouts.note: Filesystem layout segments compose automatically and persist across navigation.

dynamicRoutes.note: Bracketed segments support parameters, catch-all routes, and optional catch-all routes.

parallelRoutes.note: Named @slots have independent navigation state, loading UI, and defaults for unmatched routes.

interceptedRoutes.note: Interception conventions support routed modals with different soft-navigation and direct-link behavior.

prefetch.note: Link prefetching and router.prefetch can prepare route data and UI. Static and dynamic routes have different prefetch behavior.

softNavigation.note: App Router Link/router navigation updates the URL and replaces route segments without a full reload. Shared layouts stay mounted; loading UI and prefetching can cover server waits, but do not guarantee a latency target.
softNavigation.label: App Router

viewTransitions.note: Next.js documents an experimental React View Transitions integration. This review does not treat that experimental flag as a stable, automatically animated navigation API; application boundaries, CSS and browser support still matter.
viewTransitions.label: Experimental integration

redirects.note: Proxy can redirect or internally rewrite requests; configuration and render-time redirect APIs provide other boundaries.

serverData.note: Async Server Components load from fetch, databases, or other asynchronous I/O.

clientData.note: The guide recommends query libraries such as SWR or React Query. A client query cache is not supplied by Next.js itself.
clientData.label: SWR / React Query

requestDedupe.note: The guide documents fetch memoization and React.cache for sharing equivalent reads during rendering.

persistentCache.note: use cache retains function or component results with explicit lifetimes. Storage and coordination depend on deployment.
persistentCache.label: use cache

invalidation.note: Path/tag invalidation and cache lifetime controls support different freshness semantics.

isr.note: Regenerates cached pages by time or on demand; static-only export does not provide ISR.

apiRoutes.note: route.ts handlers use Web Request/Response and support multiple HTTP methods.

actions.note: Server Functions marked with use server can be called from Client Components and used as form actions.
actions.label: Server Functions

forms.note: Server Actions receive FormData and support pending/error feedback. Application validation or an external schema library is still required.

assessment.summary: Form transport, validation, pending feedback and optimistic state are separate behaviors; the progressive-forms and optimistic-updates rows review the latter contracts explicitly.
strengths: Server Actions receive FormData and support pending/error feedback. Application validation or an external schema library is still required.
tradeoffs: Do not infer a no-JavaScript submission path, automatic validation, accessible field errors or rollback merely from the ability to receive FormData.

middleware.note: Proxy runs before request completion for redirects, rewrites, and header logic. It is not a replacement for authorization in handlers.
middleware.label: Proxy

cookies.note: cookies() reads request cookies and writes them from Server Functions or Route Handlers. Session management remains application/library work.
cookies.label: Cookie API

cssModules.note: Imports .module.css files with generated local class names.

scopedCss.note: styled-jsx provides locally scoped styles; the App Router guide documents the required style registry.
scopedCss.label: styled-jsx

tailwind.note: Official setup instructions integrate the external Tailwind compiler and PostCSS package.
tailwind.label: Tailwind CSS

cssInJs.note: Supported libraries need Client Components and server style insertion setup; not every CSS-in-JS library supports Server Components.
cssInJs.label: Library-dependent

images.note: Image generates responsive, size-optimized output. Remote sources and deployment image services require configuration.
images.label: next/image

fonts.note: next/font self-hosts local or downloaded fonts and configures optimized loading and fallback behavior.
fonts.label: next/font

scripts.note: Script supports beforeInteractive, afterInteractive, and lazyOnload. Worker offloading is experimental.
scripts.label: next/script

assetPipeline.note: Next.js fingerprints build-managed JS, CSS, fonts, and statically imported images. Their content-based URLs can be cached for a year with immutable headers. Files placed directly in public/ retain their original names and default to max-age=0; they are not automatically fingerprinted.
assetPipeline.label: Hashed build assets

staticAssets.note: Files in public are served from the URL root; cache policy differs from fingerprinted build assets.

metadata.note: Typed Metadata covers canonical/alternate links, social cards, robots, icons, and title fields.
metadata.label: Extensive, integrated API

assessment.label: Extensive, integrated API
assessment.summary: Strong coverage of route-aware metadata and generated SEO assets, with explicit composition needed for nested objects.
strengths: Typed static metadata and async generateMetadata.
Automatic route-segment inheritance, title templates, and access to resolved parent metadata.
File conventions integrate generated social images and crawler documents.
tradeoffs: Nested objects merge shallowly. Replacing openGraph can discard an inherited description or image list.
Title templates have segment-specific rules; asynchronous metadata interacts with caching and rendering.

dynamicMetadata.note: generateMetadata can await data and resolved parent metadata; eligible fetches are memoized.

metadataInheritance.note: Layouts and pages merge root-to-leaf. Merge is shallow: a child openGraph object replaces the parent object.

metadataOverrides.note: Child keys replace ancestor keys. To retain parent OG images, read parent metadata and explicitly compose the array.
metadataOverrides.label: Shallow replacement

titleTemplates.note: Ancestor templates format child titles; title.absolute bypasses a template. A template does not format the same segment’s own page title.

socialImages.note: ImageResponse generates OG/Twitter images using a supported subset of CSS; file conventions publish them.

sitemaps.note: Structured sitemap generators support image/video entries, locales, and multiple sitemap files.

robots.note: Static robots.txt or a typed robots generator defines user-agent rules and sitemap URLs.

markdown.note: @next/mdx integrates Markdown/MDX with the App Router; remark/rehype plugins and component mapping are configurable.
markdown.label: @next/mdx

collections.note: The reviewed MDX guide covers file/content rendering and remote sources, not a typed collection loader/schema/query registry. Add application/CMS tooling for that contract.

draftMode.note: Draft Mode bypasses cached/published content for preview requests. The application must secure the enabling endpoint.

translations.note: The official guide demonstrates app-owned dictionaries and lists external translation libraries; it does not supply a message-catalog engine.
translations.label: Dictionary recipe

localeRouting.note: The App Router guide uses a [lang] segment plus application proxy logic for language detection and redirects.
localeRouting.label: Routing recipe

localeFormatting.note: next-intl provides locale-aware number and date/time formatters for Next.js applications; it is a separate package.
localeFormatting.label: next-intl

auth.note: The guide recommends an authentication library and shows application-owned session and authorization patterns. No complete identity service is bundled.
auth.label: Auth library / recipe

csp.note: Nonce-aware script handling works with application-configured CSP. Per-request nonces require dynamic rendering.

cspNonce.note: The application generates a nonce and matching CSP header; Next applies it to framework-generated scripts and supports nonce props. Per-request nonces require dynamic rendering and limit static generation, ISR and partial-prerendered shells.
cspNonce.label: Dynamic rendering required

csrf.note: Server Actions enforce POST and compare Origin with Host; allowed origins are configurable. This is not universal CSRF protection for custom endpoints.
csrf.label: Server Actions only

environment.note: Loads .env files; NEXT_PUBLIC_ values are inlined into browser bundles. Runtime server secrets remain separate.

assessment.summary: Environment visibility and enforced server-only import boundaries are separate safeguards.
strengths: Unprefixed environment values remain server-only by default; NEXT_PUBLIC values are public.
server-only imports produce a build error when consumed by client code.
tradeoffs: Explicitly returned props/action results can still leak sensitive data. Authorization and minimal DTOs remain application responsibilities.

types.note: TypeScript integration includes generated route-aware helpers and typed configuration. Type coverage is not a guarantee of runtime input validation.

hmr.note: Fast Refresh usually preserves component state; some edits trigger full reloads.

cli.note: create-next-app scaffolds projects; next provides development and production lifecycle commands.

bundleAnalysis.note: The Turbopack analyzer inspects modules and import chains; Webpack uses the optional @next/bundle-analyzer package.

unitTests.note: The documented Vitest/React Testing Library setup covers synchronous components. Async Server Components need a different strategy.
unitTests.label: Vitest / Jest

e2eTests.note: The official recipe runs Playwright against a production build, including browser navigation tests.
e2eTests.label: Playwright

observability.note: Next.js emits OpenTelemetry spans; an SDK/exporter or monitoring backend must be configured separately.
observability.label: OpenTelemetry hooks

errorHandling.note: Nested error and global-error boundaries provide fallback/retry UI; expected mutation failures are returned explicitly.

tradeoffs: Rolling deployments need compatible assets/action encryption keys and deployment IDs.
